goal: Create a concise English CLIP training and zero-shot classification framework schematic.
workingSize: 180 x 112 mm working size, landscape approximately 16:10
scope: Visual-target case run; final native reconstruction is outside this batch.
copy: Learning to match images and text
Radford et al., 2021 | Conceptual schematic; no measured scores

claims.text: Jointly train image and text encoders to match paired images and descriptions in a batch.
Project and normalize both representations. Pairwise cosine similarities feed a symmetric image-to-text/text-to-image contrastive objective.
At zero-shot inference, reuse the learned encoders to compare a query image with text prompts describing the candidate classes.
A three-pair training batch and a dog-versus-cat/car example are illustrative design choices; no measured scores or real inference are claimed.

constraints: Use exactly three paired training samples and exactly a 3-by-3 core similarity grid; do not use a different number of rows and columns.
The matched diagonal reflects paired training examples, not measured model accuracy.
Use only the requested labels/captions; small row/column IDs I1/I2/I3 and T1/T2/T3 are permitted if useful.
The source dog photo is not required; create illustrative car/dog/flower samples without calling them new CLIP results.
limits: This is a conceptual explanation with a synthetic example, not an experiment or measured output.
A selected basic single-template inference view omits ensembling and benchmark detail.
